explanation: Major ocean currents distribute thermal energy by moving heat from the equator to cooler parts of the biosphere. The Gulf Stream warms the eastern coast of North America and western Europe, while another Southern Hemisphere current warms the eastern coast of South America. In contrast, the Humboldt Current in the Southern Hemisphere carries cold water northward along the western coast of South America. During an El Niño Southern Oscillation event, the typical cold-water upwelling off the western coast of South America subsides, disrupting global climate and weather patterns.

questions.q: Which ocean current warms the eastern coast of North America and western Europe?
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Gulf Stream warms the east coast of North America and parts of western Europe.'

questions.q: What happens during an El Niño Southern Oscillation event?
opts: The Gulf Stream reverses direction and cools North America.
The cold upwelling off the west coast of South America subsides.
The doldrums move to 30 degrees latitude.
Acid rain levels double in the Southern Hemisphere.
questions.exp: The notes define El Niño Southern Oscillation as: 'Cold upwelling off west coast of South America subsides.'
